claim: The demo API's gate-run suite was red for a FIXTURE reason presented as a product failure: a test database seeded on a previous day was adopted with an exposure receipt whose two-hour window had closed, so gate_run skipped beat 4 (the admission) and every verdict read NOT PROVEN. The fixture now checks that its subject is USABLE rather than merely PRESENT, and repairs a dead receipt by issuing a new one. Beat 4 admits, the verdict is PROVEN, and it stays PROVEN on a database reused from a previous day.

mechanism: verticals/mainline/apps/demo-api/src/mainline_demo_api/scenario.py:_RECEIPT_SQL requires 'r.expires_at > now()', so an expired receipt makes resolved.receipt_id None.

verticals/mainline/apps/demo-api/src/mainline_demo_api/gate_run.py:552-553 (the lead cited :541 before W1's edits landed) - 'if resolved.check_id is None or resolved.receipt_id is None' sets beats[3]['outcome'] = 'skipped'.

A skipped beat 4 is a failure the payload records as such, so the verdict becomes NOT PROVEN. Beats 1-3 keep refusing exactly as before, which is why the failure is silent to a human watching the screen.
scripts/proof/gate_refusal.py:1154 issues the receipt with 'now() + INTERVAL '2 hours''. That is a CORRECT TTL for a fresh run.
verticals/mainline/apps/demo-api/tests/conftest.py:661 (was :650 when the lead measured it) issues the same two-hour window in the read-surface fixture.

It becomes a time bomb at the ADOPTION step: tests/test_gate_run.py's w4_database fixture adopted any database whose demo permit was still state='dispositioned' with open_blocking >= 1, and tests/conftest.py's demo_database fixture adopted any database whose w3_fixture.ready marker row was present (the lead's citation: conftest.py:756-766). Both of those survive the receipt, so a database seeded yesterday was adopted today with a dead one.
the_defect.why_the_tests_could_not_say_so: The five red tests are all about the gate. None of them was about the fixture, so all five reported 'observed outcome=skipped' and none of them said 'the exposure receipt expired 40 hours ago'. The postcondition the fixture never carried is now test_the_fixture_yields_a_subject_beat_four_can_actually_run_on, and it fails with the receipt's expiry instant in the message.
the_defect.not_a_ttl_widening: mainline.exposure_receipt constrains only 'expires_at > issued_at' (0061_exposure_receipt.sql:75, CONSTRAINT ttl_bounded). The bound the lead pointed at - 0066_disposition.sql:183-185, CONSTRAINT ttl_enforced, 'expires_at <= signed_at + max_ttl_hours * INTERVAL 1 hour' - is on mainline.disposition and not on the receipt. So the receipt's window COULD have been widened without hitting a CHECK. It was not widened: two hours is what the product does, and a fixture that modelled a twelve-hour exposure would be asserting against a system nobody ships. The fix is in the adoption test and the repair, not in the number.

the_fix.why_the_repair_is_an_insert: mainline.exposure_receipt carries an append_only weld - 0128d_trg_refuse_mutation_exposure_receipt.sql:28, 'CREATE TRIGGER append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON mainline.exposure_receipt' - which raises P0001 for every UPDATE and every DELETE, for every role. Extending an expired window in place is refused by the schema. Issuing a new receipt is also what the product itself asks for: 0102_fn_disposition_project.sql:123-125 raises 'MAINLINE: exposure receipt absent or expired - re-materialise before signing'. This is asserted against the running database, not read off the migration, by test_an_expired_receipt_is_repaired_by_issuing_one_not_by_editing_one.
tests_added_to_test_gate_run.py: test_a_subject_whose_receipt_expired_is_gate_ready_and_not_beat_four_ready - the defect as a predicate: state and open_blocking, the two things the old adoption test looked at, BOTH survive the receipt.
test_a_consumed_subject_is_reported_as_consumed_not_as_an_expiry - the four unmet conditions are distinguished, because they have different remedies.
test_the_fixture_yields_a_subject_beat_four_can_actually_run_on - the postcondition the fixture never carried. False on any scratch database more than two hours old before this change.

test_an_expired_receipt_is_repaired_by_issuing_one_not_by_editing_one - proves P0001 on UPDATE and on DELETE against the live database, then re-issues inside a transaction and rolls it back, asserting the live receipt is unchanged afterwards.
